full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nizamul Huq, J: These two rules in Civil Revision No.4381 of 1999 and 4382 of 1999 were issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 31.05.1999 passed by the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla in Title Appeal Nos.112 of 1997 and 113 of 1997 allowing the appeals and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 29.6.1997 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Comilla in Title Suit No.1 of 1996 and Title Suit No.36 of 1996 respectively should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. At the time of issuance of the rules, the operation of the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal Nos.112 of 1997 and 113 of 1997 were stayed. 

2. As the facts of the cases are similar, they arise out of single judgment passed in both the appeals and also in both the suits heard analogously, this judgment and order also will cover both the two rules. 

3. The petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.1 of 1996 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chandina, Comilla, against the defendant opposite parties contending inter alia that one Abdur Rahim was the owner of the suit land and he was in possession for more than twelve years and the said Abdur Rahim on the basis of a registered deed of exchange dated 13.11.1984 exchanged with the plaintiff and the plaintiff got .30 acres of land and possession thereto and continued possession for more than twelve years and mutated his name in new Khatian No.489 in the said lands. The defendants have got no right title and possession in the suit land but threatened dispossession of the suit land on 29.12.1995 and as such the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.1 of 1996 for permanent injunction. 

4. The defendant opposite party Nos.1, 3 and 4 filed written statement in the Title Suit No.1 of 1996 denying all the materials allegations made in the plaint and contended inter alia that Asker All was the original owner of the suit land measuring 1.99 acres and he left behind one son Abdur Rahim and two daughters Titama Bibi and Bishama and 17 decimals of land was acquisitioned by highway and Abdur Rahim sold .35 decimals to Ekor Ali Mia, .20 decimals to Aboni Mohon, .10 decimals to Lolit Mohan, .27 decimals to Waresh Mia, .22 decimals to Ali Ahmed and .15 decimals to Elahi Box. As such Abdur Rahim sold 1.16 acres while he was owner of .99 decimals, and became title less. Then in order to grab the share of sisters Titama and Bishama, Abdur Rahim created forged deed by forging their names and then they filed criminal case against Abdur Rahim. To be saved from conviction, the said Abdur Rahim executed a nadabi deed and registered it on 28.9.1985 admitting that he has no claim in .90 decimals of land out of 1.63 acres, .62 decimals from dag No.1101 and 1.01 acres from dag No.1102 and also admitted that Titama and Bishama are owners and possessors therein. Later said Abdur Rahim and plaintiff Kazi Sultan Ahmed collusively executed the ewaj deed dated 13.11.1984 in order to grab the lands of Titama and Bishama and they in order to cancel the said ewaj nama, filed Title Suit No.59 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chandina, and notices were duly served upon Kazi Sultan Ahmed and Abdur Rahim and Titama and Bishama got ex-parte decree dated 16.05.1989 in the suit and aforesaid exchange deed was cancelled. Bishama has sold her share to Titama and Titama is now in possession of their land by giving barga to Elahi Box. Abdur Rahim had no right to exchange the suit land with the plaintiff and the plaintiff got no title on the basis of that exchange deed.

5. The plaintiff then filed Title Suit No.36 of 1996 contending inter alia that Abdur Rahim being the owner of the suit land exchanged it with the plaintiff by exchange deed dated 13.11.1984 and the plaintiff got his possession in the suit land. But when his right, title and interest was challenged, the plaintiff Kazi Sultan Ahmed filed Title Suit No.1 of 1996 praying for restraining the defendant No.2 from interfering with his possession in the suit land and then by filling written statement, the defendant claimed about the ex-parte decree passed in title Suit No.59 of 1998 against the plaintiff. The plaintiff asserted that he had no knowledge about the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.59 of 1998 and no notice of the suit was served upon him. The defendant obtained the said ex-parte decree by practicing fraud upon the Court and the ex-parte decree is liable to be set aside. 

6. The Title Suit No.36 of 1996 was contested by defendant opposite party No.1 by filing written statement contending inter alia that the deed of exchange dated 13.11.1984 was cancelled in the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.59 of 1988 Abdur Rahim had no interest or right to exchange the lands because before that he sold all of his shares in the lands to different persons by registered deeds. Considering that aspect the exchange deed No.120258 dated 31.11.1984 was cancelled in title Suit No.59 of 1988. It was contended in the written statement that 24 decimals of land has been recorded in the name of defendant Titama correctly and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

7. As both suits contain common question of facts and law, so the trial Court heard the suit analogously. 5(five) witnesses were examined on behalf of the plaintiff side while the defendant side examined 7(seven) witnesses in favour of them. Both sides produced documentary evidence also. On consideration of the evidence adduced both oral and documentary, the Trial Court decreed both the suit by its judgment and decree dated 29.6.1997. 
8. Against the said judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, the defendant opposite party nos.1-3 as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.112 of 1997 and defendant opposite party No.1 as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.113 of 1997 before the District Judge, Comilla. The appeals, were transferred to the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla for disposal who after hearing the parties and perusal of the records by judgment and decree dated 31.5.1999 allowed the appeals and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. As such both the suits were dismissed. Against the said judgments and decrees passed by the Court of appeal, the plaintiff as petitioner filed revisional applications in this court and obtained these rules. 

9. Mr. Amir Hossain with Ms. Shahnaz Haque, the learned Advocate appeared for the plaintiff petitioner while Mr. Md. Nur Hossain Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appeared for the defendant Opposite Parties in both the rules. 

10. Mr. Amir Hossain has placed both the revisional applications and the impugned judgments passed by the Courts below and submitted that the learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record and the cases of the parties arrived at a correct decision that in the suit for permanent injunction the plaintiff has established the claim of permanent injunction and rightly decreed the suit on that and also the learned trial court found that no notice was served 
upon the plaintiff in Title Suit No.59 of 1988 and as such he rightly decreed that suit setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.59 of 1988 but the Court of appeal without reversing the findings of the trial court and without considering the evidence on record committed an error of law resulting in an error in such order occasioning failure of justice in dismissing both the suits by allowing both the appeals. The learned Advocate for the petitioner 
further submitted that the Title Suit No.36 of 1996 that is the suit for setting aside the decree of Title Suit No.59 of 1988, the trial Court considered that the summons were not served upon the plaintiff petitioner rather it was served upon another person and the learned Court of appeal also found that but even then erroneously arrived at the decision that the notice upon the plaintiff 
was properly served and dismissed the suit for setting aside the decree which has caused 
failure of Justice. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submitted that the plaintiff by producing documents have established claim and possession of .30 decimals of land on the basis of the exchange deed, which the defendant witness also admitted by way of admitting possession of Abdur Rahim before exchange and it follows possession of the plaintiff after exchange but the learned Court of appeal rejected the claim of the plaintiff on the ground that the exchange deed is a void one and that the petitioner could not prove his possession in the case land and dismissed the suit on that which has caused failure of justice. He further submitted that mere registration outside the domain of the proper sub registry office does not make the deed illegal but even then the court of appeal found that the ewaj deed is illegal and dismissed the suits which has caused 
failure of justice. 

11. On the other hand the learned Advocate for the Opposite Parties submitted that the court of appeal on consideration of the evidence and materials on record rightly arrived at the findings that the plaintiff could not prove prima facie title and exclusive possession in the suit land and as such the suit for permanent injunction was rightly dismissed. Further more the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submitted that the learned Court of appeal found that 
the plaintiff has no interest over the .30 decimals of land because already he sold all the lands belonging to him except 10 decimals of land and he exchanged that showing that he got .30 decimals of land in exchange of 10 decimals of land but the exchange deed was not registered in 
accordance with law and is void one and as such the case of the plaintiff was rejected by the court of appeal and there is nothing to interfere with the finding of the court of appeal in this respect as such the suit was dismissed. The learned Advocate for the Opposite party further submitted that in the ex-parte decree of Title Suit No.59 of 1988,the learned Court clearly found that notices was rightly served upon the petitioner and as such the Court of appeal arrived at the conclusion that the ex-parte decree cannot be set aside and rightly dismissed the suit of the plaintiff and by this decree the plaintiff has suffered no failure of justice and as such judgment and decree passed by the Court of appeal cannot be interfered by this Court. Lastly he submitted 
that the findings of facts arrived at by the Court of appeal being final court of appeal of fact, cannot be interfered in the revisional jurisdiction without any specific finding of misreading and misassesment of the evidence on record, and there being no allegation of that, the judgment and decree passed by the learned Court of appeal cannot be disturbed in this revisional jurisdiction, and thus the rules are liable to be discharged. 

12. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the evidence and materials on record. It is admitted that the deed of exchange-dated 13.11.1984 contains the properties belonging to Chandina, sub-registry office. It is also admitted that the said exchange deed was executed in Joint Sub-registry office, Comilla. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed the section 28 of the registration Act 1908 which reads as follows: 

28(1) Save as in this part otherwise provided, every document mentioned in section 17, sub-section (1) clause (a), (b), (c), (d) and (e), sectionl7, sub-section (2), and section 18, in so far as such documents affects immoveable property shall be presented for registration in the office of a Sub-Registrar within whose sub-district the whole or [major portion] of the property to which such document relates is situate. 

Provided that where the major portion of such property is not situate within one sub district the document shall be presented for registration in the office of the Sub-Registrar within whose sub district any portion of such property is situate. 
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub section (1), 
(a) after a document is registered, no party thereto shall be entitled to question the validity of its registration on the ground that the property which purported to give jurisdiction to the Sub-Registrar to register it either did not exist or was fictitious or insignificant or was not intended to be conveyed; and 
(b) a document the registration of which secured by the inclusion of a non-existent, fictitious or insignificant portion or item shall not in any manner affect the rights of a person who was not a party thereto and acquired rights in the property without notice of the transaction to which such document relates. 

13. The lands of the instant exchange deed belongs to Chandina Sub-Registry office and as such the deed ought to have been registered in Chandina Sub-Registry office. But it has been registered at Joint Sub-Registry office, Comilla which had no legal authority to register it. As such the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that any party of that deed is not entitled to raise any question as to its validity is not sustainable in law because the deed in question has not been registered containing the properties did not exist or was fictitious or insignificant or was not intended to be conveyed rather the facts remains that Joint Sub-Registry office, Comilla was not authorized to register the deed with the properties mentioned in the deed. In the instant case the deed itself has become void. In this respect the case of Shefali Rani and other versus Makhon Chandra Das and others reported in 50 DLR Page 349 may be considered wherein it has been found that when the question was registered at a place by a sub-registrar where no portion of the property mentioned in the document was situated within the jurisdiction of that sub-registrar the document was wholly void. The court of appeal in accepting this decision passed by this court and as such the exchange deed stands void resulting to the effect that plaintiff had no interest in 30 decimals of land as claimed by him. The court of appeal 
has also considered and found that Abdur Rahim had no saleable interest for exchanging .30 decimals of land. The learned court of appeal has considered the exhibits placed before that Court and found that the deed of exchange is affected for want of title of the executor being owner of 28 acres of land after sale of lands on different days and Abdur Rahim was not 
authorized to exchange this with .30 acres of land. Moreover the Court of appeal considered that both the lands of exchange deed are nal and of equal status and as such .30 decimals of land cannot be exchanged with .10 decimals of land and no reason for that exchange has been stated. The finding of the Court of appeal to the effect that the exchange deed has not been registered in the proper office leads to the conclusion that the exchange deed is void on the ground that it 
is ineffective and lacks in jurisdiction. As such it cannot be questioned because it is supported by law and facts. The submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the District Registrar has got authority to register the deeds of the lands within his jurisdiction and the instant deed being registered in the Comilla District, should be accepted to be proper. The court of appeal considered that submission and rejected on the ground that it has not been registered by 
the district Registrar, rather it has been registered by joint sub-registrar and they are not of equal right and equal status. The petitioners could not show any notification authorizing the joint sub-register, Comilla to register the deeds of Chandina sub-registry and as such I am also of the view that the finding of the court of appeal that as there was no land of the jurisdiction of Comilla 
sub-registry office in the deed, the deed exhibit I is void and Mega'. Coming to the next point, the Court of appeal has considered evidences of the witnesses and on consideration of those of plaintiff witness Nos.1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, the Court of appeal came to the specific finding that the plaintiff could not prove their prima facie title and conclusive possession in the suit land. This 
being a finding of fact, this Court sitting in revisional jurisdiction cannot interfere in this finding and as such the Title Suit No.1 of 1996, a suit for permanent injunction on the finding to the effect that plaintiff could not prove title and conclusive possession over the suit land cannot be decreed and the Court of appeal rightly dismissed the said Suit No.1 of 1996 there is nothing to 
interfere in the said judgment and decree passed by the court of appeal, and as such it is affirmed. 

14. As regards suit for cancellation of the ex-parte decree, that is Title Suit No.36 of 
1996, the court of appeal clearly found that the notice of the Title Suit No.59 of 1988 was sent through registered post and defendant Kazi Sultan received that on 18.8.1988 by putting his own signature and the normal notice was received by his brother Joynal Abedin as the said defendant 
was out side and his brother agreed to receive that and then it was served upon him on 28.8.1988 resulting service of notice upon the said defendant, the instant plaintiff of the suit and the notice was received by the full brother of the plaintiff who stay in the same house and mess with the plaintiff and on this the court of appeal clearly found that the notices were duly served upon the defendant of Title Suit No.59 of 1988, the plaintiff of title Suit no.36 of 1996. Moreover the plaintiff has no where stated that the signature of available in the receipt is not of him and has not made any allegation against the post office peon and even Joynal Abedin could have been produced to state that he did not receive the notice for his brother. This finding being finding of fact, and noting could be placed by the learned Advocate for the petitioner to this court to find that the Court of appeal has misread or misappeciated the evidence on record and as such the said finding cannot be set aside. Thus I am of the view that the notice of Title Suit No.59 of 1988 was duly served upon the plaintiff in Title Suit No.36 of 1996 and as such the Title Suit No.36 of 1996 for setting aside the ex-parte decree of title Suit No.59 of 1988 cannot be decreed. The learned court of appeal rightly found that and dismissed the suit. On consideration of the judgment and decree passed by the Court of appeal and also on consideration of the findings of fact arrived at by the Court of appeal, I am of the view that the court of appeal has not committed any error of law resulting in an error in such decree occasioning failure of justice and as such it has rightly allowed the appeal and dismissed both the suits. 

15. The rules thus merit no consideration and both the Rules are hereby discharged with costs. The judgment and decree passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla in Title Appeal Nos.112 of 1997 and 113 of 1997 are affirmed and the Title Suit No.1 of 1996 and Title Suit No.36 of 1996 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Chandina, Comilla stands dismissed. The stay order passed at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby vacated. 

16. Send down the lower court records along with a copy of the judgment immediately.

End.
